question: Does the positive conditional association between effective colony number at year t and growth from t to t+1 persist after conditioning on recent demographic momentum?

base_model.response: log1p abundance growth from t to t+1
base_model.predictor: standardized log1p effective colony number at t
controls: standardized current log1p abundance at t

lag1.complete_case_rule: exclude transitions lacking t-1 positive abundance

lag1_lag2.complete_case_rule: exclude transitions lacking either lagged growth

held_out_evaluation.comparison: baseline with momentum controls versus the same baseline plus N_eff
held_out_evaluation.role: effect-size context only; the earlier synchronized year-block test already rejected a robust predictive interpretation

structured_null_reuse.important: This is not a new N_eff null family.
structured_null_reuse.independent_island_shift: Reuse the exact full-series island-wise circular-shift generator and seed from PALMER_NEFF_CIRCULAR_SHIFT_V1; shift the complete N_eff sequences first, then fit the momentum-conditioned complete-case sample.
structured_null_reuse.joint_shift: Reuse the exact 26 x 16 full-series group: one common lag for CHR/COR/HUM/TOR and an independent LIT lag. Do not redefine the permutation group after dropping early lag-ineligible rows.

reporting.interpretation: Assess whether demographic momentum materially attenuates the association. Do not restore a predictive or causal claim.

boundaries: No claim that lag controls remove all time-varying confounding.
No new topology metric, threshold, climate window, or null family is opened by this sensitivity.
The held-out gain is descriptive because the previously frozen synchronized block test already failed.
